# One declaration, one work unit per partition

A `fan_out` block splits the node's claim into sub-claims and dispatches one
work unit per partition. The parent settles on their aggregate verdict.

## The deployment

```yaml
root: /workspace
host: 127.0.0.1
grpc_port: 9200
http_port: 9210
sweep_interval_seconds: 60
```

## The template

```yaml
name: fanout-parallel
version: v1
nodes:
  - type: partitioned
    executor: verifier-http
    claim_producers:
      - name: claim-producer-filesystem
        selector: data
        intent: rw
        alias: parent
    error_types:
      "acquire/unavailable":
        action: give_up
    fan_out:
      claim: parent
      partition_request: '{"list":[{"key":"p1"},{"key":"p2"},{"key":"p3"}]}'
      parallelism: 3
      error_policy:
        kind: strict
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          url:
            type: string
            default: "http://endpoint:18999/slow"
```

No per-partition node, no external splitter.

## What the product does

The producer's split returns one sub-scope per declared partition — the
`subclaim.acquired` event reports `sub_scope_descriptor_count: 3` — and the
dispatch records three sub-claims keyed `p1`, `p2`, `p3`.

All four runs — the parent and its three clones — settle fresh.

## The partitions run at the same time

Point the work units at an endpoint that holds each request open and reports the
peak number in flight. With `parallelism: 3` the endpoint sees a peak of three
in flight and three served.

Change nothing but the knob:

```yaml
      parallelism: 1
```

The endpoint sees a peak of one, and the same three served. The overlap is
rimsky's dispatch, not something the endpoint did.

## The parent settles on the aggregate

The parent's settlement follows the last sub-claim's resolution in event order:
it waits for the partitions rather than racing them.

Point the work units at an endpoint answering 500 for every partition. No run
settles fresh, the parent settles failed, the event log carries
`terminal/error/aggregate/strict_failed`, and the partitions' claims are
abandoned (`claim_resolution.abandon`) rather than committed.

A failed fan-out leaves no half-committed work behind.
